# vendor/ — third-party material: what we may carry, and how we attribute what we may not

<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->

This repository is MIT-licensed (see `LICENSE`). The things it studies are not.
This directory is the ledger of every upstream whose work shaped a statement
in `specs/`, `investigations/` or `lab/`, with the copyright holder, the
licence, the revision we read, and the rule we apply to it.

## Three classes of material

| Class | Example | What we do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Public domain or MIT-compatible** | 47 CFR text (US Government work, 17 U.S.C. § 105); MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD Rust crates | May be carried verbatim under `vendor/<source>/` with its attribution. Today only the CFR text is carried (`vendor/cfr47/`). |
| **Redistributable but not MIT-compatible** | GPL-2.0 kernel modules and GPL-3.0 applications (Scale RF software, `quadrf-mesh`, `gr-lora_sdr`, Meshtastic, KrakenSDR software); CC BY-SA 4.0 antenna design files | Never copied into this repository; never linked into our binaries. Used as separate processes behind documented IPC, or rebuilt unmodified from the upstream tree in `resources/`. Attributed in `vendor/<source>/ATTRIBUTION.md`; restated in our own words in `vendor/summary/`. |
| **Not redistributable** | Datasheets (© Analog Devices, Semtech, Skyworks, Raspberry Pi Ltd); the vendor schematic PDF ("source-available for debugging"); the proprietary FPGA bitstream; vendor web pages | Kept only in gitignored `resources/`. Facts we rely on are restated in `vendor/summary/` with page references, and in `specs/` as behaviour statements. |

`vendor/summary/` is the catch-all: every copyright that is not declared
compatible with MIT is honoured by restatement and attribution there, never by
reproduction.

## Layout

| Path | Upstream | Licence (SPDX) | Carried verbatim? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cfr47/` | Code of Federal Regulations, Title 47 (LII mirror of the e-CFR) | Public domain (US Government work) | Yes: section text, regenerated by `scripts/vendor-cfr.py` |
| `scalerf/` | Scale RF Inc. — QuadRF software stack, antenna design files, schematic PDF, web documentation, FPGA bitstream | GPL-2.0 (kernel modules, SoapySDR module, GUI, CLI), GPL-3.0 (packaging default, GNU Radio demos), CC-BY-SA-4.0 (antenna files), proprietary (bitstream, RF core) | No |
| `radioroy-quadrf-mesh/` | radioroy — `quadrf-mesh` LoRa-compatible PHY and Meshtastic daemon for QuadRF | GPL-3.0 | No |
| `tapparel-gr-lora_sdr/` | J. Tapparel et al., EPFL TCL — `gr-lora_sdr` | GPL-3.0 | No |
| `meshtastic/` | Meshtastic LLC and contributors — firmware, protobufs, documentation | GPL-3.0 (firmware, protobufs); documentation per site notice | No |
| `krakenrf/` | KrakenRF Inc. — KrakenSDR hardware documentation, `heimdall_daq_fw`, `krakensdr_doa` | GPL-3.0 (software); documentation per wiki | No |
| `analog-devices/` | Analog Devices (Maxim Integrated) — MAX2850, MAX2851, MAX2871 datasheets (all three in hand) | Proprietary | No |
| `raspberry-pi/` | Raspberry Pi Ltd — RP1 Peripherals datasheet, Pi 5 documentation | Proprietary datasheet; documentation CC-BY-SA-4.0 | No |
| `semtech/` | Semtech — SX1261/2 datasheet, SX1262 and LR1121 product data | Proprietary | No |
| `skyworks/` | Skyworks Solutions — SKY65404-31 LNA datasheet, SE5004L-EK1 evaluation-kit datasheet | Proprietary | No |
| `rust-crates/` | crates.io crates we intend to depend on | MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD unless noted (noted: `meshtastic` GPL-3.0, `librtlsdr-rs` GPL-2.0) | No (dependencies are fetched by Cargo and locked) |
| `alpine/` | Alpine Linux packages used on copal | Per package | No |
| `summary/` | Our restatements of all of the above | MIT (ours) | — |

## Rules

1. Each `ATTRIBUTION.md` names: copyright holder, licence with SPDX id, URL,
   the revision read (commit hash or document revision and date), the files
   or pages read, what we use from it, and what we are not permitted to do.
2. A statement in `specs/` that depends on an upstream cites the `resources/`
   path; the matching `vendor/summary/` file carries the attribution so the
   repository is correct even with `resources/` deleted.
3. Trademarks (ScaleRF, QuadRF, MoonRF, Meshtastic, KrakenSDR, LoRa) are used
   nominatively to identify the products; no endorsement is implied.
4. Adding an upstream means adding its row here, its `ATTRIBUTION.md`, its
   `vendor/summary/` file, and its manifest row in `docs/resources-manifest.md`.
